t: This is 17 to 19 Cockspur Street, a building in Westminster. It was designed by Aston Webb, a British architect best known for the principal facade of Buckingham Palace and the main building of the Victoria and Albert Museum. He often worked in partnership with Ingress Bell, and he served as president of the Royal Academy from 1919 to 1924. He was also the founding chairman of the London Society. So as you look at this building, you're looking at the work of an architect whose name is attached to some of the most prominent frontages in the capital.
